rules.title: Define the core job
rules.action: Write the user's desired outcome as a job-to-be-done before proposing a page.
rules.verify: The brief names a concrete task and success condition, not a vague aesthetic.

rules.title: Map primary segments
rules.action: Separate first-time, returning, expert, and accessibility-dependent user needs when they materially differ.
rules.verify: Flows identify which segment each decision serves.

rules.title: Locate the critical journey
rules.action: Draw the shortest credible path from entry to task completion before polishing secondary pages.
rules.verify: The main journey is testable end-to-end.

rules.title: List user questions
rules.action: Capture what users need to know at each decision and surface that information before commitment.
rules.verify: A participant can act without searching for hidden conditions.

rules.title: Distinguish evidence from guess
rules.action: Mark observed problems, analytics findings, and design hypotheses separately.
rules.verify: Each recommendation has an evidence level or a test plan.

rules.title: Interview for behavior
rules.action: Ask about the last real attempt and observed workarounds rather than opinions about imagined features.
rules.verify: Notes contain concrete episodes and obstacles.

rules.title: Study failure cases
rules.action: Research abandonment, errors, slow networks, and help requests, not only successful happy paths.
rules.verify: Journey map includes at least three plausible failures.

rules.title: Define decision metrics
rules.action: Choose a leading task metric and a guardrail before changing the interface.
rules.verify: Measurement plan has denominator, baseline, and ownership.

rules.title: Prioritize by impact
rules.action: Rank issues by user harm, reach, frequency, and remediation effort rather than visual novelty.
rules.verify: Critical blockers precede stylistic changes.

rules.title: Validate with target users
rules.action: Test representative tasks with actual users when practical; do not equate internal preference with evidence.
rules.verify: Findings record observed behavior and unresolved questions.

rules.title: Organize by user tasks
rules.action: Group destinations around user goals, not database entities or team structure.
rules.verify: A person can predict where a task belongs.

rules.title: Use familiar labels
rules.action: Prefer language the audience recognizes over internal acronyms and clever category names.
rules.verify: Navigation labels are understood without tooltips.

rules.title: Show current location
rules.action: Expose active item, page title, and hierarchy where applicable.
rules.verify: Users can answer where they are and how to return.

rules.title: Limit top-level choices
rules.action: Keep primary destinations to a manageable set; group related secondary areas instead of a flat mega-menu.
rules.verify: Main navigation has no indistinguishable duplicates.

rules.title: Preserve back behavior
rules.action: Ensure back navigation restores meaningful context, selection, and scroll when appropriate.
rules.verify: Going back does not unexpectedly discard progress.

rules.title: Provide robust search
rules.action: Offer search when content density warrants it, with tolerance for common terms and useful results.
rules.verify: Queries produce understandable matching and zero-result states.

rules.title: Offer clear filters
rules.action: Distinguish filtering from sorting, show active constraints, and make reset easy.
rules.verify: Users can see and remove applied filters.

rules.title: Use breadcrumbs selectively
rules.action: Provide hierarchical breadcrumbs for deep information spaces, not as a substitute for clear navigation.
rules.verify: Each crumb maps to a meaningful ancestor.

rules.title: Design empty destinations
rules.action: Explain why a page has no content and offer the next valid action.
rules.verify: The empty state never strands users.

rules.title: Prevent dead-end pages
rules.action: Provide recovery routes from missing records, access denial, and invalid URLs.
rules.verify: Users can navigate onward without browser refresh.

rules.title: Start with content hierarchy
rules.action: Prioritize reading and actions before choosing grids or breakpoints.
rules.verify: Small screens retain the essential task.

rules.title: Use fluid containers
rules.action: Combine max-width boundaries with fluid widths rather than fixed desktop-only canvases.
rules.verify: Content fits narrow and wide screens.

rules.title: Choose content breakpoints
rules.action: Adapt when components stop working, not solely at standard device widths.
rules.verify: Intermediate widths have no awkward clipping.

rules.title: Protect readable line length
rules.action: Constrain long text measures and use suitable line height for scanning.
rules.verify: Paragraphs stay comfortable on wide screens.

rules.title: Make spacing systematic
rules.action: Establish spacing tokens and use them consistently for related and unrelated content groups.
rules.verify: Like relationships have like spacing.

rules.title: Respect safe areas
rules.action: Avoid covering essential controls with notches, system bars, browser chrome, or bottom gestures.
rules.verify: Edge devices retain tappable controls.

rules.title: Handle long strings
rules.action: Plan for long names, numbers, translations, and unbroken identifiers without truncating critical meaning.
rules.verify: Layout survives worst-case text fixtures.

rules.title: Use grid and flex intentionally
rules.action: Choose layout primitives matching content semantics; avoid absolute positioning for ordinary document flow.
rules.verify: Resizing preserves order and reachability.

rules.title: Avoid horizontal overflow
rules.action: Prevent page-level sideways scrolling except for deliberate and accessible data views.
rules.verify: A 320 CSS-pixel viewport remains navigable.

rules.title: Test zoom and reflow
rules.action: Check 200% zoom and narrow-screen reflow without losing task-critical content.
rules.verify: Controls and information remain available under magnification.

rules.title: Use a type scale
rules.action: Define a small hierarchy of body, supporting, section, and headline styles using tokens.
rules.verify: Heading levels and visual sizes are consistent.

rules.title: Write outcome-led headings
rules.action: State the user task or result before branding or decorative language.
rules.verify: First-screen heading identifies the page purpose.

rules.title: Prefer plain language
rules.action: Replace jargon and ambiguous verbs with words the audience understands.
rules.verify: Labels are clear without a glossary.

rules.title: Make button labels specific
rules.action: Name the action and likely result, such as Save changes, instead of generic Continue when avoidable.
rules.verify: Users can predict the next step.

rules.title: Keep helper text persistent
rules.action: Place important formatting rules near the input rather than only in placeholders.
rules.verify: Guidance remains visible after typing.

rules.title: Surface restrictions early
rules.action: State prices, limits, eligibility, and prerequisites before users invest effort.
rules.verify: No material surprise appears at submission.

rules.title: Write humane errors
rules.action: Explain the specific issue and correction without blame, jargon, or humor at the user's expense.
rules.verify: The error suggests a clear recovery.

rules.title: Use meaningful truncation
rules.action: Truncate only secondary text and preserve identifying information through expansion or full-label access.
rules.verify: Users can distinguish similar items.

rules.title: Format values locally
rules.action: Use locale-aware dates, money, units, and separators; include units and time zones where material.
rules.verify: Values are unambiguous to the target audience.

rules.title: Make skimming effective
rules.action: Use descriptive section labels, parallel lists, and front-loaded facts.
rules.verify: A scanning reader finds the key answer quickly.

rules.title: Establish one focal point
rules.action: Make the primary action and information dominant through scale, contrast, or placement.
rules.verify: First glance indicates what matters.

rules.title: Use contrast with purpose
rules.action: Make contrast express hierarchy, action availability, and important status, not just decoration.
rules.verify: Essential elements remain discernible.

rules.title: Reserve accent colors
rules.action: Apply brand accents to the most meaningful interaction and status surfaces.
rules.verify: Every element does not compete for attention.

rules.title: Use semantic status tokens
rules.action: Separate success, warning, danger, info, and neutral states from raw palette values.
rules.verify: Status changes remain coherent across themes.

rules.title: Avoid color-only meaning
rules.action: Pair colored indicators with labels, patterns, icons, or programmatic meaning.
rules.verify: Meaning survives grayscale and assistive use.

rules.title: Build light and dark themes
rules.action: Test contrast and elevation independently in each theme instead of inverting colors mechanically.
rules.verify: Neither theme hides boundaries or text.

rules.title: Use elevation sparingly
rules.action: Apply shadows, borders, and layering to show interaction and containment.
rules.verify: Surface hierarchy remains readable without deep shadows.

rules.title: Align optical details
rules.action: Fine-tune icon and label centering, baseline, and stroke weight while preserving semantic alignment.
rules.verify: Repeated rows and controls look visually coherent.

rules.title: Maintain icon semantics
rules.action: Use familiar icons with labels for ambiguous actions; keep an icon family consistent.
rules.verify: Icons do not require guessing.

rules.title: Favor brand restraint
rules.action: Apply gradients, blur, and glow only when they enhance identity without hiding controls.
rules.verify: Reduced effects retain a professional interface.

rules.title: Create semantic tokens
rules.action: Define roles for text, surfaces, borders, focus, and feedback instead of scattering raw color values.
rules.verify: Theme updates require few central edits.

rules.title: Tokenize spacing and type
rules.action: Centralize spacing, typography, radius, and elevation choices.
rules.verify: Components share predictable values.

rules.title: Reuse native controls
rules.action: Prefer the existing design library and platform primitives before making custom components.
rules.verify: New UI matches established interaction patterns.

rules.title: Define variant intent
rules.action: Give components clear size, importance, and destructive variants rather than arbitrary style combinations.
rules.verify: Each variant has a valid use case.

rules.title: Specify complete states
rules.action: Design default, hover, focus, active, loading, disabled, success, error, and empty states where relevant.
rules.verify: State matrix covers key components.

rules.title: Separate behavior from styling
rules.action: Preserve keyboard semantics, validation, and state machines while allowing visual variants.
rules.verify: Styling changes do not regress interaction behavior.

rules.title: Name components by role
rules.action: Use names such as PrimaryButton or StatusBadge rather than colors or page coordinates.
rules.verify: Components remain meaningful after redesign.

rules.title: Document composition rules
rules.action: Define which components can nest, which can stretch, and where complex patterns belong.
rules.verify: Engineers avoid ad hoc compositions.

rules.title: Support design token evolution
rules.action: Introduce aliases or migrations for renamed tokens rather than breaking unrelated screens.
rules.verify: Existing consumers stay functional.

rules.title: Track reusable patterns
rules.action: Promote repeated page patterns into shared components only after stable use cases emerge.
rules.verify: Abstraction reduces duplication without erasing differences.

rules.title: Ask only essential fields
rules.action: Remove or defer nonessential inputs and explain why sensitive details are required.
rules.verify: Every required field maps to a genuine task need.

rules.title: Use correct input types
rules.action: Match email, phone, date, numeric, and autocomplete semantics to the expected value.
rules.verify: Mobile keyboards and autofill are appropriate.

rules.title: Always label inputs
rules.action: Pair each control with a persistent accessible label and helpful instructions.
rules.verify: Placeholder text is not the only label.

rules.title: Group related fields
rules.action: Use logical sections and fieldsets to clarify dependencies and reduce perceived effort.
rules.verify: Users can scan each section's purpose.

rules.title: Validate at useful moments
rules.action: Validate after sufficient user intent rather than flashing errors during partial entry.
rules.verify: Incomplete typing does not create noise.

rules.title: Preserve entered values
rules.action: Keep valid data and user edits after errors, reloads where appropriate, and recoverable submission failures.
rules.verify: Retry never forces unnecessary re-entry.

rules.title: Link errors to fields
rules.action: Show specific inline messages and, for long forms, an actionable summary that targets invalid controls.
rules.verify: Users reach every error by keyboard.

rules.title: Show process progress
rules.action: Expose steps, saved state, and exit/resume affordances for lengthy workflows.
rules.verify: Users know remaining effort and can return safely.

rules.title: Guard destructive submission
rules.action: Use confirmation or undo based on reversibility and impact, without duplicating needless prompts.
rules.verify: Accidental irreversible actions have protection.

rules.title: Handle double submission
rules.action: Disable or idempotently handle repeated requests and reconcile server feedback with button state.
rules.verify: Duplicate taps do not create duplicate operations.

rules.title: Give immediate acknowledgement
rules.action: Show pressed, busy, or changed state promptly for relevant interactions.
rules.verify: Users never wonder whether a tap registered.

rules.title: Use button compression selectively
rules.action: Start with scale 0.95 on touch-down and damped spring to 1 on release; adjust to existing design language.
rules.verify: Press feels tactile without layout movement.

rules.title: Add physical refresh resistance
rules.action: For pull-to-refresh, test initial list displacement near 35% of finger travel and cap overscroll; signal threshold.
rules.verify: List does not travel one-to-one or trigger accidentally.

rules.title: Roll changed digits responsibly
rules.action: Stagger meaningful digit changes around 100 ms while keeping a readable formatted final number available.
rules.verify: Changes do not misrepresent financial values.

rules.title: Make reorder pickup explicit
rules.action: Start with a 1.05 lifted scale and approximately 200 ms sibling shifts; provide non-drag alternatives.
rules.verify: Destination and order remain clear.

rules.title: Animate card expansion spatially
rules.action: Try 350 ms ease-out while managing focus, scroll, interruption, and reduced-motion equivalents.
rules.verify: Expanded content is immediately operable.

rules.title: Sequence success confirmation
rules.action: Use circle then checkmark within approximately 470 ms only after confirmed success.
rules.verify: Visual and accessible status agree.

rules.title: Use shared motion tokens
rules.action: Standardize quick, normal, and expressive durations and corresponding easings.
rules.verify: Components do not mix arbitrary physics.

rules.title: Honor reduced motion
rules.action: Replace nonessential movement with opacity or instant state transitions while retaining informative feedback.
rules.verify: Prefers-reduced-motion users finish the same task.

rules.title: Prevent animation races
rules.action: Cancel or reconcile transitions on rapid re-click, navigation, errors, unmounts, and incoming state updates.
rules.verify: State remains truthful under interruption.

rules.title: Build semantic structure
rules.action: Use real headings, landmarks, lists, buttons, links, and form controls before adding ARIA.
rules.verify: Accessibility tree reflects visible structure.

rules.title: Support keyboard completely
rules.action: Make all functions reachable and operable without a pointer, with logical focus progression.
rules.verify: End-to-end keyboard task is possible.

rules.title: Make focus visible
rules.action: Show a high-contrast visible focus indicator and never hide it without a robust replacement.
rules.verify: Tab navigation is easy to track.

rules.title: Manage modal focus
rules.action: Focus the active dialog, contain focus appropriately, support Escape when safe, and restore focus on close.
rules.verify: Screen-reader and keyboard users do not lose position.

rules.title: Meet text contrast
rules.action: Target WCAG 2.2 AA: at least 4.5:1 for ordinary text and 3:1 for qualifying large text.
rules.verify: Automated and manual contrast checks pass.

rules.title: Provide usable target sizes
rules.action: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA target-size minimum or its documented exceptions; aim larger for touch comfort.
rules.verify: Dense toolbars remain usable without precise pointing.

rules.title: Avoid dragging-only actions
rules.action: Provide a simple-pointer and keyboard-operated way to achieve any reorder or drag function unless truly essential.
rules.verify: A user can complete the action without dragging.

rules.title: Announce dynamic outcomes
rules.action: Use scoped, appropriate live updates for confirmations, errors, and async status without announcement spam.
rules.verify: Assistive users learn the important outcome.

rules.title: Provide media alternatives
rules.action: Add captions to meaningful audio, transcripts where appropriate, and relevant alt text for informative images.
rules.verify: Content remains understandable without its primary sensory channel.

rules.title: Validate with assistive tech
rules.action: Check zoom, screen reader, keyboard, contrast, reduced motion, and forced colors as relevant.
rules.verify: At least one manual assistive-tech path is reported, or explicitly untested.

rules.title: Prioritize thumb reach
rules.action: Keep frequent primary controls reasonably reachable and avoid edge conflicts with system gestures.
rules.verify: One-handed core tasks remain comfortable.

rules.title: Use visible affordances
rules.action: Make interactive surfaces look actionable rather than depending on hidden swipe knowledge.
rules.verify: First-time users discover the primary operation.

rules.title: Pair gestures with controls
rules.action: Offer visible buttons or menus for swipe, long-press, and drag operations.
rules.verify: Every important action has a discoverable alternative.

rules.title: Handle virtual keyboard
rules.action: Keep focused inputs, validation messages, and submit actions visible above the software keyboard.
rules.verify: Forms remain usable while typing.

rules.title: Prevent accidental taps
rules.action: Space adjacent destructive and routine actions and avoid tiny low-separation targets.
rules.verify: Typical touch errors are recoverable.

rules.title: Respect platform conventions
rules.action: Follow native back, navigation bars, sheets, and system UI patterns when they fit the app.
rules.verify: The interface behaves as users expect on each platform.

rules.title: Use progressive disclosure
rules.action: Collapse supporting detail while retaining key information and accessible paths on narrow screens.
rules.verify: Main task never depends on desktop-only content.

rules.title: Design offline transitions
rules.action: Explain loss of connectivity and distinguish locally queued work from server-saved work.
rules.verify: Users know if action is really completed.

rules.title: Manage orientation changes
rules.action: Reflow rather than resetting forms, search context, scroll, or selection.
rules.verify: Device rotation does not destroy progress.

rules.title: Test real-device feel
rules.action: Check scroll, touch latency, haptics when supported, gesture competition, and on-screen keyboard on devices.
rules.verify: Performance is not judged solely by desktop emulation.

rules.title: Lead with decisions
rules.action: Show the question and decision each metric supports before choosing a chart style.
rules.verify: Every dashboard tile has a reason to exist.

rules.title: Name metrics precisely
rules.action: Define units, periods, comparison basis, and calculation assumptions near key KPIs.
rules.verify: Users can interpret a number without guessing.

rules.title: Preserve accurate scales
rules.action: Use appropriate axes and avoid misleading truncation, especially for bars and comparisons.
rules.verify: Values cannot be visually overstated.

rules.title: Provide context for deltas
rules.action: Show baseline, percentage versus absolute change, and the comparison period.
rules.verify: A positive or negative change has interpretable meaning.

rules.title: Use suitable chart forms
rules.action: Pick bars for discrete comparison, lines for trends, and tables for exact lookup rather than novel ornament.
rules.verify: Intended insight is easy to extract.

rules.title: Represent missing data
rules.action: Distinguish zero, not available, pending, suppressed, and not applicable.
rules.verify: The viewer cannot confuse absent data with actual zero.

rules.title: Offer data table alternatives
rules.action: Provide textual or tabular access to chart content for keyboard, screen reader, and precision use.
rules.verify: No key insight depends only on graphics.

rules.title: Make filters transparent
rules.action: Display applied time range, segments, data freshness, and any inherited filters.
rules.verify: Export and visible values use the same scope.

rules.title: Design dense tables deliberately
rules.action: Keep headers clear, preserve sorting meaning, and make row actions discoverable on small screens.
rules.verify: Users can compare values and act without losing row context.

rules.title: Use restrained numeric motion
rules.action: Animate values only when meaningfully updated and avoid decorative rolling for volatile live financial figures.
rules.verify: Motion cannot imply false precision or completion.

rules.title: Demonstrate value early
rules.action: Help users perform the first meaningful task before requesting optional setup.
rules.verify: Time to first value is measurable.

rules.title: Ask permission in context
rules.action: Request notifications, location, contacts, or camera access only when the user understands the benefit.
rules.verify: Permissions are not demanded on first launch without explanation.

rules.title: Allow exploration where safe
rules.action: Offer guest, preview, or sample content when account creation is not technically essential.
rules.verify: Prospects can understand the product before committing.

rules.title: Make pricing transparent
rules.action: State recurring charges, trials, renewal conditions, and cancellation paths before purchase.
rules.verify: No material fees are hidden behind the final step.

rules.title: Minimize checkout friction
rules.action: Prefer straightforward fields and guest checkout where supported; do not force unnecessary account creation.
rules.verify: Purchase can complete with minimal interruptions.

rules.title: Provide a clear primary CTA
rules.action: Give one obvious primary next step per decision surface while retaining honest alternatives.
rules.verify: Users know what clicking will do.

rules.title: Avoid deceptive urgency
rules.action: Do not fabricate countdowns, inventory scarcity, or social proof.
rules.verify: Every urgency claim has verifiable underlying data.

rules.title: Show onboarding progress
rules.action: Use clear checkpoints, skip options for optional tasks, and realistic completion expectations.
rules.verify: Users can recover or return later.

rules.title: Confirm next steps
rules.action: After signup or payment, show status, receipt or reference, and what happens next.
rules.verify: Users do not need to guess if the action succeeded.

rules.title: Measure ethical outcomes
rules.action: Track completion, comprehension, and satisfaction with conversion, not clicks alone.
rules.verify: Improvement does not rely on dark patterns.

rules.title: Optimize real interaction speed
rules.action: Measure responsiveness and long tasks on target devices before adding effects.
rules.verify: Delayed interactions are addressed at source.

rules.title: Protect core content loading
rules.action: Prioritize visible primary content, compress assets, and avoid unnecessarily blocking render.
rules.verify: Essential task appears promptly on slow connections.

rules.title: Reserve layout space
rules.action: Specify media dimensions and stable placeholders to reduce content jumps.
rules.verify: Loading does not displace the user's target unexpectedly.

rules.title: Use honest loading states
rules.action: Distinguish skeleton, spinner, queued, saving, and completed states based on actual lifecycle.
rules.verify: UI never claims server success prematurely.

rules.title: Design meaningful retry
rules.action: Offer retry with preserved context and explain when an operation may have already succeeded.
rules.verify: Retrying cannot easily duplicate side effects.

rules.title: Support stale data labels
rules.action: Show freshness or sync state when cached content may differ from current truth.
rules.verify: Users can distinguish cache from current data.

rules.title: Avoid expensive animations
rules.action: Prefer compositor-friendly transforms and opacity, and minimize forced layout during gestures.
rules.verify: Low-end device interaction remains smooth.

rules.title: Handle no-JS or partial-failure
rules.action: Where appropriate, provide functional fallback, progressive enhancement, or a clear recovery path.
rules.verify: Critical task is not silently blank after an error.

rules.title: Use lightweight assets
rules.action: Load responsive media, subset payloads, and defer offscreen extras without harming accessibility.
rules.verify: Payload matches user context.

rules.title: Measure Core Web Vitals appropriately
rules.action: For web, watch field LCP, INP, and CLS with context rather than treating lab scores as business results.
rules.verify: Regression checks include field or realistic lab evidence.

rules.title: State data use plainly
rules.action: Explain why personal information is needed at the point of collection.
rules.verify: Users can make an informed choice.

rules.title: Default to least privilege
rules.action: Request only necessary permissions and avoid unnecessary sharing by default.
rules.verify: Sensitive capabilities are restricted.

rules.title: Make consequences explicit
rules.action: Explain irreversible actions, audience visibility, and external effects before final confirmation.
rules.verify: The user understands who or what is affected.

rules.title: Avoid dark patterns
rules.action: Do not use disguised ads, hidden opt-outs, forced continuity, or shame-based copy.
rules.verify: Rejecting an optional offer remains straightforward.

rules.title: Show authentic proof
rules.action: Use real reviews, verified security claims, and authentic testimonials only.
rules.verify: Trust badges are backed by evidence.

rules.title: Protect sensitive content
rules.action: Mask or omit secrets in UI, logs, screenshots, examples, and clipboard affordances.
rules.verify: Test fixtures contain no real credentials.

rules.title: Confirm destructive scope
rules.action: Name affected records and permanence; favor undo when safe.
rules.verify: Users cannot easily delete the wrong item unnoticed.

rules.title: Distinguish authority levels
rules.action: Make read-only, admin-only, external, and destructive features clear in UI.
rules.verify: Unauthorized actions do not appear as false promises.

rules.title: Avoid misleading defaults
rules.action: Never preselect paid extras, consent, or risky actions without an appropriate user choice.
rules.verify: Default choices do not exploit inattention.

rules.title: Design trustworthy AI states
rules.action: Distinguish generated suggestions from verified facts, expose uncertainty and human override where needed.
rules.verify: Users know what is automated and can correct it.

rules.title: Externalize UI strings
rules.action: Keep user-facing copy out of code and use translation keys with context.
rules.verify: Text can be translated without code changes.

rules.title: Use logical CSS properties
rules.action: Prefer inline-start, inline-end, and writing-direction-aware layout over hard-coded left/right for directional UI.
rules.verify: RTL layouts do not require duplicate stylesheets.

rules.title: Mirror directional affordances
rules.action: Adapt navigation arrows, step sequence, and directional motion where semantics require it; do not mirror brand marks.
rules.verify: Back and forward remain intuitive in RTL.

rules.title: Support mixed-script text
rules.action: Handle Arabic-English mixed labels, phone numbers, codes, and identifiers with controlled bidi isolation.
rules.verify: Number and product-name ordering stays correct.

rules.title: Avoid fixed text dimensions
rules.action: Expect expansion and different glyph metrics across languages.
rules.verify: Long translations do not clip controls.

rules.title: Localize data formats
rules.action: Apply locale rules for numbers, money, dates, calendar systems if relevant, and pluralization.
rules.verify: Screen examples display correct regional conventions.

rules.title: Choose language deliberately
rules.action: Detect preference cautiously, allow explicit switching, and preserve language choice.
rules.verify: Users can override automatic language detection.

rules.title: Respect regional address forms
rules.action: Adapt state/province, postal code, and phone structure instead of hard-coded US assumptions.
rules.verify: Users can submit valid local information.

rules.title: Test fonts and diacritics
rules.action: Verify script coverage, line height, truncation, and glyph rendering in multilingual themes.
rules.verify: Arabic diacritics and long names are legible.

rules.title: Keep translations contextual
rules.action: Review verbs, error messages, and cultural metaphors for local meaning, not word-for-word equivalence.
rules.verify: Native-language reviewers understand the intended action.

rules.title: Create scenario coverage
rules.action: Test the happy path plus empty, error, pending, disabled, interrupted, and permission-denied states.
rules.verify: Each crucial flow has a documented scenario matrix.

rules.title: Test representative viewports
rules.action: Review narrow phone, large phone, tablet, and desktop dimensions relevant to the product.
rules.verify: Breakpoint transitions show no visual regressions.

rules.title: Use realistic fixture data
rules.action: Include long names, high totals, zero records, large lists, and slow responses.
rules.verify: Layout and behavior survive edge-case content.

rules.title: Check keyboard workflows
rules.action: Complete the primary journey with Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, and Escape where appropriate.
rules.verify: No keyboard trap or invisible focus remains.

rules.title: Run automated accessibility scans
rules.action: Use existing lint and accessibility test tools as a first pass, then do manual checks.
rules.verify: No unsupported claim of full accessibility compliance is made.

rules.title: Test real performance
rules.action: Use a throttled network and constrained CPU/device for critical flows.
rules.verify: Interaction feedback remains responsive under stress.

rules.title: Compare before and after
rules.action: Capture stable screenshots or behavioral recordings of changed areas when tools permit.
rules.verify: Review shows meaningful difference without unintended drift.

rules.title: Document design decisions
rules.action: Record chosen patterns, alternatives, tradeoffs, and exceptions concisely.
rules.verify: Future engineers can understand why decisions were made.

rules.title: Measure experiments responsibly
rules.action: Define hypothesis, population, primary metric, guardrails, and stopping rules before A/B testing.
rules.verify: Results are not interpreted from vanity metrics.

rules.title: Report honest completion
rules.action: Distinguish shipped changes, recommendations, executed tests, blocked tests, and remaining risks.
rules.verify: Stakeholders know exactly what was verified.
